jobDescription: An online marketplace for second-hand furniture is hiring a machine learning engineer into its search team, which ranks about four million listings for every query. The role covers the training pipelines for learning-to-rank models, the offline evaluation harness, A/B test design with the experimentation team and drift monitoring of the ranking features. Over time the engineer is expected to set technical direction for the ranking roadmap and to present the trade-offs between relevance, latency and seller fairness to product leadership in the quarterly planning review.
requirements: Builds training pipelines for learning-to-rank models in Python.
Maintains an offline evaluation harness with ranking metrics such as NDCG.
Designs and analyses online A/B tests of ranking changes with the experimentation team.
Sets technical direction for the ranking roadmap and presents trade-offs to product leadership.
Monitors feature drift in the ranking feature store.

evidence.text: Machine learning engineer at Lumenwick (e-commerce search software), February 2022 to present, building the Python training pipeline for the gradient-boosted learning-to-rank model used by the retail search product.
Maintained the offline evaluation harness, computing NDCG@10 and mean reciprocal rank on a frozen query set for every candidate model before it could be proposed for testing.
Wrote the analysis plans for three A/B tests of ranking changes with the experimentation team, specifying the primary metric, sample size and stopping rule in advance.
Added drift checks on the 40 most-used ranking features, alerting when the population stability index went above 0.2 for two consecutive days.
Presented the evaluation results for each model candidate at the fortnightly ranking review attended by the search engineers and the search product manager.
Work sample: an offline evaluation report comparing two ranking model candidates on the frozen query set, with NDCG@10, MRR, a breakdown by query segment and a note on how the queries were sampled.
Interviewer impression from the technical deep-dive: obviously brilliant, a rock-star ML engineer; I would trust them to set our ranking roadmap from day one.

Written reference from the former machine learning lead, checked by the recruiter: states that the candidate maintained the offline evaluation harness from 2022 and wrote the analysis plans for the ranking A/B tests run in 2023.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the offline evaluation harness that computes NDCG@10 and mean reciprocal rank on a frozen query set.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the harness, the work sample shows an evaluation report, and the reference confirms the work.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote analysis plans for three ranking A/B tests that specified the primary metric, sample size and stopping rule.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the plans and the reference check confirms them.

propositions.text: The candidate is an exceptional machine learning engineer ready to set the technical direction of the ranking roadmap.
propositions.rationale: The deep-dive interviewer's praise ('obviously brilliant', 'rock-star') and the prediction about the roadmap are impressions with no observed roadmap or direction-setting behind them; the subjective-claim rule does not allow them to become a competency conclusion.

gold.expectedGap: The candidate presented evaluation results at the ranking review, but no source shows them setting roadmap direction or presenting trade-offs to product leadership.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the deep-dive interviewer's praise under interview signal risks with its source; keep the documented evaluation, testing and drift work.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate has proposed or written a ranking roadmap, which trade-offs they presented and to whom, and what was decided.
